question.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
question.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{v,w\}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set $\{v,w\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-2)\cdot (-3)+(-2)\cdot 2+(-9)\cdot 1}{(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}v=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-2)\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 2+(-9)\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}w=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
